# Dionysus AI Video Editor

> A browser video editor (works on phones, including iOS Safari) that turns a storyboard JSON planned by your own AI into a production to-do list and a timeline. Dionysus makes no AI calls itself: the user's AI writes the storyboard, and the user generates and uploads the clips.

To plan a storyboard for Dionysus, read the storyboard guide first and reply with one JSON code block in its format.

## Storyboard planning

- [Storyboard guide](https://ckfun0skf.github.io/dionysus-ai-video-editor/ai/storyboard-guide.md): the dionysus.storyboard/1 (v1.1) JSON format and how it becomes a video, how to choose presets, the preset ids you may use (grouped by category), the numbered rules and an example
- [Storyboard guide as a web page](https://ckfun0skf.github.io/dionysus-ai-video-editor/ai/storyboard-guide.html): the same guide as HTML
- [Presets](https://ckfun0skf.github.io/dionysus-ai-video-editor/ai/presets.json): machine-readable preset ids, categories, descriptions, params with defaults and usage hints

## Long stories

For a long video, don't write one huge JSON: agree an outline first, then reply with part 1 (a complete storyboard with the first batch of shots) and then one part per message ({ "format", "part": { "index", "of", "after" }, "shots", … }, no "meta"); the user imports each part and Dionysus merges it by id. See the guide's rule "long-story-parts".

## Series

A project can be an episode of a Series: a shared library of characters, props, locations and styles. The user's prompt then ends with a SERIES ASSETS list. Reuse those assets by id with { "id": "<id>", "seriesRef": "<id>" } instead of redefining them, and give a new recurring asset "series": true so later episodes can reuse it. See the guide's rules "series-reuse", "series-promote" and "series-tools". With WebMCP, call list_series_assets first.

## WebMCP tools

When the user turns on agent access (Storyboard → Agent) in a browser with WebMCP, the open Dionysus tab registers these tools. Use them instead of writing JSON; every call is validated by the guide's rules (a rejected call changes nothing) and is one undo step for the user.

- `get_guide` · read-only: The Dionysus storyboard guide: how the format becomes a video, every field, the preset ids you may use, the numbered rules and an example. Read it before editing.
- `get_storyboard`(id) · read-only: Without "id": a summary (title, counts, the shot list with ids, durations and titles, asset ids, cue ids). With "id": the full JSON of that shot, asset ("<asset>@<state>" for a state), audio cue, or "meta" / "connections".
- `create_storyboard`(meta, assets, shots, audio, connections): Start a new storyboard when there is none: "meta" (title, aspect, style, …), any "assets", and at least one shot. Add the rest with add_shot. Fails if a storyboard exists (edit it instead).
- `update_meta`(patch): Change storyboard "meta" fields (title, aspect, style, fps, textStyles, audioOutput { mode: stereo | binaural, environment?: room | outdoor }, …).
- `add_asset`(asset): Add an asset (character, location, prop, style, image, frame, video, audio or html).
- `update_asset`(id, patch): Change fields of an asset (name, prompt, references, qa, aspect, source, states, …).
- `remove_asset`(id): Remove an asset. Rejected while a shot, layer, cue or other asset still uses it (the error lists where); change those first.
- `add_asset_state`(asset, state): Add another look of an asset (lamp on, coat soaked, street at night), used as "<asset>@<state>".
- `update_asset_state`(asset, id, patch): Change fields of an asset state (name, prompt, references, qa).
- `add_shot`(shot, after): Add a shot. "after": the shot id to insert after (omit to append at the end; null to insert first). Add a long story in batches of shots.
- `update_shot`(id, patch): Change fields of a shot (title, description, durationSec, clip, inSec, dialogue, qa, render, effects (each may set applyTo: main, overlay or all), …). Schema 3.1: a shot has no prompt; change the prompt, references, camera, keyframe or genDurationSec of its clip with update_asset (a shared clip changes every shot that uses it).
- `remove_shot`(id): Remove a shot, its connections and its own (auto) clip. Rejected while a cue, last-frame link or other shot still needs it; change those first.
- `set_shot_layers`(id, layers): Replace all layers of a shot (text, html, image, video), drawn in order on top. [] removes them. Text layers may set anim.inParams, e.g. the typewriter cursor { cursor, blink, after: blink|hide|fade, scramble }. A layer is linked to its shot's main clip on Send to timeline unless it sets link: false (RULE 46).
- `set_shot_background`(id, background): Give a still shot a colour or gradient background (sets "render": "still"); null removes it. Use clip or background, not both.
- `set_shot_params`(id, params, replace): Set the params of an html shot's clip (e.g. a title card's text). Merged into the current values; null removes one; "replace": true replaces them all.
- `reorder_shots`(id, index, order): Move one shot ("id" + 0-based "index") or give the whole new "order" (every shot id once).
- `set_connection`(connection, remove): Set the connection between two adjacent shots (kind cut / continuity / match, note, transition). "remove": true deletes it.
- `add_cue`(cue): Add an audio cue (voiceover, music, sfx, ambience, sting, dialogue) that plays from a shot: an audio "asset", or "source": { "fromVideo", "inSec"?, "outSec"? } to use the sound of a video asset or of a shot's clip. Gets "audio<n>" as id when you give none.
- `update_cue`(id, patch): Change fields of an audio cue (from, to, atSec, volume, fades, loop, volumeKeys, fx, position { azimuth, distance, width? }, pan, positionKeys, source { fromVideo, inSec?, outSec? }, …).
- `remove_cue`(id): Remove an audio cue.
- `list_series_assets` · read-only: List the shared assets of the Series this project belongs to (id, type, name, short description, states). Reuse them with use_series_asset instead of defining a new character, prop, location or style.
- `use_series_asset`(id, as): Add a Series asset to the board, linked: its definition, states and uploads come from the Series and stay in sync. Then use its id (or "<id>@<state>") in shots.
- `promote_to_series`(id): Add a board asset to the project's Series so later episodes can reuse it (sets "series": true; the app adds it with its uploads and links it). If the Series already has that id, the board links to it (dedupe by id).
- `validate` · read-only: Run the importer's checks on the current storyboard and list its warnings (edits are already checked; this reports what is left to improve).
- `export_json` · read-only: The whole storyboard as storyboard JSON ("dionysus.storyboard/1"), edits included.
- `send_to_timeline`(mode): Update the timeline from the storyboard (mode "update", the default): adds shots that have a clip and new audio cues, switches changed clips and refreshes shot text; everything else on the timeline stays. Shots without a clip yet go on as placeholders at their planned length (RULE 59), and a shot that now has a clip replaces its placeholder in place. New layers and in-shot cues are linked to their shot's main clip (moved, trimmed and deleted with it) unless they set link: false. Update does not change the length of clips already placed: after changing shot durationSec (e.g. new voice files) use mode "relayout" (P62, RULE 77): it updates, then gives every shot clip the length Send would give it now, packs the main track again (gaps kept), re-places the layers, captions and effects of shots whose length changed and every story audio cue at the board's offsets, and keeps the clips' own edits (volume, effects, transform, transitions, pins). Mode "replace" clears the timeline and sends the whole board again (manual timeline edits are lost; Undo restores). One undo step; returns counts.
- `sync_to_storyboard`: Write timeline edits back to the storyboard (one undo step): clip lengths, order and trims, layers, effects and audio cues of the shots they came from. Timeline clips with no shot become new shots, layers or cues flagged needsPrompt; shots whose clip was removed are kept and flagged removedFromTimeline. Afterwards call list_needs_prompt and fill every item.
- `list_needs_prompt` · read-only: List the shots, layers and audio cues flagged needsPrompt (made on the timeline by Sync to Storyboard). Fill each: a shot needs a description (update_shot) and a clip generation prompt on its clip asset (update_asset), a layer or cue needs a description (set_shot_layers / update_cue); filling it clears the flag.
- `plan_insert_shots`(after, lastShotDescription, insertJson): P21 "Plan with AI" for Insert shot after. Without "insertJson": returns the planning prompt for inserting shots after shot "after" (last-shot description, neighbouring shots, every asset and clip with generated or not, the guide rules and the strict answer format). With "insertJson" ({"schema":"3.1-insert","insertAfter","shots","newAssets","audio"?}): validates it with the importer and inserts the shots after "after" with the new assets, in one undo step; the following shots are renumbered.
- `revise_storyboard`(brief, shotId, reviseJson): P36 "Revise with AI" / "Edit with AI". Without "reviseJson": returns the revise prompt for the problem in "brief" (whole storyboard, or only shot "shotId"), with the guide rules and the strict answer format. With "reviseJson" ({"schema":"3.1-revise","shots","add","remove","assets","newAssets","audio"?}, or with "shotId" {"schema":"3.1-shot-revise","shotId","shot","assets","newAssets"}): validates it (only what it changes or adds can block; existing board issues are listed, not blocking) and merges it by id in one undo step. Generated assets keep their versions; removed shots leave their timeline clips in place.

### Timeline review and edit tools

The same tab also registers tools that read, review and edit the timeline itself (times in seconds; each edit is one undo step and returns the clip). See rule "review-timeline".

- `get_timeline` · read-only: The timeline as JSON: settings (size, fps), duration, and every track (id, kind, group, main) with its clips (id, start/duration/in in seconds, asset, type, volume, effect, transform, text, link parent, storyShot, version, pinnedVersion, mask). Times are seconds. version is the take showing now; pinnedVersion is set when this clip stays on that take instead of following the storyboard. mask, when present, is a clip visibility mask (source-picture fractions; key times in seconds) — not an effect limit and not a tracker box mask (that stays on tracks[].mask).
- `capture_frame`(timeSec, maxWidth) · read-only: Render the composited frame at timeSec exactly as export would and return it as a JPEG image (maxWidth px wide, default 640, at most 1280).
- `capture_shot_frame`(shotId, frameOf, slotId, atSec): Storyboard frame references ("frameOf", RULE 50): grab the frame at atSec of the source shot's selected clip and store it as the picked frame (a PNG version with { frameOf, atSec, sourceVersionId }) of the target shot's frameOf reference. Give "shotId" (the target shot) and, when it has several frame references, "frameOf" (the source shot) or "slotId". atSec defaults to the reference's atSec. Fails when the source shot has no clip yet (generate it first). One undo step; returns the state and the PNG.
- `contact_sheet`(count, interval, maxWidth) · read-only: One JPEG grid of frames across the whole timeline, each labelled with its time. Give "count" (frames, default 12, max 36) or "interval" (seconds between frames). Use it to review the cut at a glance.
- `review_lint`(minClipSec, media) · read-only: List review problems with times and clip ids: storyboard items needing a prompt, shots removed from the timeline, very short clips, gaps and black frames, overlay clips not linked to a main clip, audio clipping or long silence, text off the frame, and missing media. Fix them with the edit tools, then run it again.
- `move_clip`(id, startSec, trackId): Move a clip to startSec, optionally onto another track (trackId of the same kind). Linked layers move with a main clip. One undo step; returns the clip.
- `trim_clip`(id, edge, atSec, ripple): Move a clip's left or right edge to atSec on the timeline. ripple: true closes/opens the gap on the main track. One undo step; returns the clip.
- `import_subtitles`(text, trackId): Add pasted SRT or WebVTT text as subtitle cues (each cue a text clip). Without trackId a new subtitle layer is created; with trackId the cues are pasted onto that existing text track and inherit its Caption style. Cues need a 00:00:01,000 --> 00:00:03,000 timing line. One undo step; returns the number of cues.
- `add_blank_clip`(track, atSec, color, durationSec): Add a solid colour clip at atSec: track "main" inserts it on the main track (later clips move up like any insert), "overlay" puts it on the first overlay layer with room (else a new one). color is #rrggbb; durationSec defaults to 3. To change the colour later call set_blank_color. One undo step; returns the clip.
- `add_code_effect`(assetId, atSec, durationSec, applyTo): Add an effect clip that runs a code package with "role": "effect" (get_timeline lists it under assets with "role": "effect") from atSec for durationSec (default 3) on the Effects layer. applyTo "main" (default) changes the main track before overlays and text; "all" changes the finished frame. Each frame the package gets that picture as ctx.source. A package of another role is rejected. One undo step; returns the clip.
- `set_code_transition`(clipId, assetId, durationSec): Use a code package with "role": "transition" on the cut into clipId (a main-track clip that starts where another ends). It draws ctx.from (outgoing) and ctx.to (incoming) over ctx.progress 0 → 1. durationSec defaults to 0.5 (each clip gives at most half of itself). A package of another role is rejected. One undo step; returns the clip.
- `set_clip_input`(clipId, input, source): A code clip's manifest "inputs" are references (numbers only, as ctx.inputs[name]) of three types: "graphic" (a picture: { luma, avgColor, motion, histogram[16] }; sources: "program" = the picture under the clip (default), a video track name, "track:<id>" or "clip:<id>" of a main or overlay clip), "audio" (a sound: { rms, peak, bands[8], onset, envelope }; sources: "mix" = everything you hear (default), an audio-carrying track or clip) and "tracker" ({ x, y, width, height, scale, rotation, found }; sources: "none" (default), "clip:<clip id>#<tracker id>" from get_timeline tracks[], or "clip:<clip id>#@<tracker name>" for a tracker the user still has to set (found:false until it exists)). The older type names "scene", "beat" and "track" mean graphic, audio and tracker. Bindings store ids, so renaming a track keeps them. source omitted = back to the default. One undo step; returns the clip.
- `rename_track`(trackId, name): Rename a track (get_timeline lists track ids and names). Names are for people and for set_clip_input; bindings use the id, so nothing breaks. 1-40 characters. One undo step.
- `track_clip`(clipId, region, atSec, fromSec, toSec, trackId, name, followers, mask): Host-side region tracker (classic template matching with a scale search, not AI subject segmentation; best on high-contrast features that stay in view). Adds a new tracker ("Track 1", "Track 2"…; a clip can have several, each independent) or re-analyses trackId. region = the box to follow on the frame at atSec (default: the range start), as fractions 0-1 of the video frame { x, y, w, h } (x/y = top-left). The box grows and shrinks with the feature. fromSec / toSec (timeline seconds inside the clip) limit the tracker to part of the clip (default: whole clip); outside that range and on lost frames (the feature left the picture or the match is too weak) there is no position: code inputs get found:false, followers hold, an inside mask hides the clip. followers = clip ids (text, photo, overlay, code) that follow the box; mask "inside" / "outside". One undo step; returns the tracker id, frames, unstable and lost counts and a few positions.
- `get_track`(clipId, trackId, everySec) · read-only: Positions of tracker trackId on clipId (trackId may be omitted when the clip has one tracker) every everySec seconds (default 0.5) across its range: { t, found, x, y, width, height, scale, conf } with x/y the box centre and width/height its size as fractions 0-1 of the output frame, scale vs the first box, conf 0-1. found:false rows (lost or weak) carry no position.
- `attach_track`(clipId, targetId, trackId, atSec, scale): Make clipId (text, photo, overlay or code clip overlapping the tracker's range) follow tracker trackId of targetId (trackId required when the target has several). Its current offset from the box, measured at atSec, is kept; scale follows the changing box size unless scale is false; rotation follows the target clip. Lost / out-of-range frames get no key (the follower holds). Written as x/y/scale keyframes you can still edit. One undo step; returns the clip.
- `set_track_mask`(clipId, trackId, mask): Traveling mask from tracker trackId of clipId: "inside" shows the clip only inside the box (hidden where the feature is lost or outside the range), "outside" cuts the box out, "off" removes it. One undo step; returns the clip.
- `set_track_range`(clipId, trackId, fromSec, toSec, name): Set tracker trackId's range on clipId to fromSec–toSec (timeline seconds inside the clip). Shrinking drops the analysis outside the new range; extending analyses only the new part, starting from the box at the old edge. Optional name renames the tracker. One undo step; returns the tracker.
- `list_unused_assets` · read-only: What Clean up project would offer: "unused" = assets nothing uses (no clip, code effect or transition, storyboard slot or shot, binding of a used code clip, or source of a used asset), and "oldVersions" = versions of kept assets that are not selected and that nothing points at. Pass the ids you choose to delete_assets.
- `delete_assets`(assetIds, versions): Remove unused assets (assetIds) and old versions (versions: [{ assetId, versionId }]) that list_unused_assets reports; anything still in use is refused with the reason. One undo step (Clean up project). Their files are freed after the next start.
- `set_blank_color`(clipId, color): Set the colour (#rrggbb) of a blank clip (get_timeline shows "blank": "#rrggbb" on it). One undo step; returns the clip.
- `audio_prompt`(name, brief, durationSec) · read-only: Returns the prompt that asks an AI for a sound or music clip in the dionysus.audioclip/1 JSON format (rendered in the browser to WAV). Pass the JSON reply to create_audio.
- `create_audio`(json, atSec): Render a dionysus.audioclip/1 JSON clip (the AI's reply to audio_prompt, or your own) to WAV, import it as an audio asset and add it on an audio track at atSec (default: 0). Invalid JSON is rejected with the problems listed. One undo step; returns the clip.
- `slip_clip`(clipId, inSec, moveLinked): Show a different part of the source inside a video, audio or HTML clip: set the source in point to inSec. The clip keeps its timeline position and length; inSec is clamped so the range stays inside the media. moveLinked: true slips linked audio/overlays by the same amount. Images and text cannot slip. One undo step; returns the clip.
- `replace_clip_asset`(clipId, assetId, onShort, fit, inSec, ripple, mode): Swap the media of a clip for another asset of the same kind, keeping every other property (position, length, effects, links). The in point is kept when it fits, otherwise moved earlier. If the new source is shorter than the clip, pass onShort: "shorten" (clip ends with the source) or "hold" (keep length, freeze the last frame); without it the call fails and explains. One undo step; returns the clip. On a shot placeholder (get_timeline "placeholder": true) any video, image or html asset fills it in place. On a main-track clip that came from a storyboard shot, the asset is added as a new version of that shot and pinned to THIS clip only (split halves and copies stay on their takes). If the new take is longer than the clip/shot, pass fit "trim" (keep the shot length; inSec picks the start, default 0) or "full" (use the whole take; later clips move when ripple is true); without fit the call fails and explains. A shorter take shortens the clip (ripple follows ripple). mode "new" (default) adds a version; mode "replace" overwrites the clip's current take in place (other clips showing that take update).
- `split_clip`(id, atSec): Split a clip at atSec (inside it). One undo step; returns both halves.
- `delete_clip`(ids, ripple): Delete one or more clips (and the layers linked to them). ripple: true closes the gap on the main track. One undo step.
- `set_clip_props`(id, volume, transform, effect, fades, speed, blend, text, position, positionKeys, pan, trackPosition, audioOutput): Change a clip in one undo step: volume (0..2), transform { x, y, scale, rotation, opacity } (null resets), effect { preset, params } (effect clips only; videoEffect preset ids and param ranges as in get_guide), fades { inSec, outSec }, speed (0.25..4), blend, text (text clips only: { text, size, color, … }); P14 sound position (clips with sound): position { azimuth -180..180 (0 front, -90 left, 90 right, ±180 behind), distance 0..1 (0 at the ear, 1 ≈ 20 m), width? 0..1 (1 keeps a stereo file's own image) } or null (centre, unprocessed), pan -1..1 (shorthand: azimuth = pan × 90), positionKeys [{ t: seconds from the clip start, azimuth, distance }] or null, trackPosition (default for the clip's track) and audioOutput { mode: stereo | binaural, environment?: room | outdoor } (whole project). Values are never clamped: an unknown preset, param, field or an out-of-range value fails the whole call with the reason and nothing changes. Returns the clip.
- `promote_overlay`(clipId, mode, position, keepTransform): Move a video, image or HTML clip from an overlay track onto the main track. mode "replace" (default) keeps its time and replaces what the main track shows there: covered main clips are removed, partly covered ones are trimmed, and a clip spanning it is split (the right part continues at the right in point). mode "insert" puts it in at its start and ripples later main clips (and their linked layers) by its duration; if it starts inside a main clip, give position "before" or "after" that clip (the call fails without it). Blend mode and chroma key are dropped; the transform is kept unless keepTransform is false; its audio is kept. One undo step; returns the main track.
- `merge_layer_up`(trackId, targetTrackId, resolve, dryRun): Move every clip of trackId into the layer directly above it on screen in the same group (the one drawn over it; or targetTrackId, which must be in the same group) and remove the emptied layer, the same as the Merge up button on a layer. Clips keep their times. If a moved clip overlaps a clip on the target, the call fails and lists the conflicts unless resolve is given: "shift" moves the incoming clip later to the first gap that fits, "trimExisting" cuts the existing clip away under it, "trimIncoming" keeps only the parts of the incoming clip that fall in gaps, "pushLater" ripples the existing clips later. resolve is one value for all or { clipId: value } per clip. dryRun returns the conflicts without changing anything. One undo step; returns the target layer's clips.
- `insert_clip_after`(assetId, afterClipId): Insert a video, image or html asset on the main track immediately after afterClipId (a main-track clip id from get_timeline). Later main clips move later by the new clip's length, and gaps after the insert keep their length. Layers and subtitles linked to those clips (link.parent, including captions sent with a shot) keep their offset from the clip they belong to; a layer with no link stays put. An audio asset, or a code package whose role is effect or transition, is rejected. One undo step; returns the new clip. In the editor the same action is "Insert new clip after current clip": current clip is the selected main-track clip (one selection), or the selected main clip under the playhead when several main clips are selected (otherwise the earliest selected), otherwise the main clip under the playhead, otherwise the nearest main clip that ends at or before the playhead.
- `paste_clips`(clipIds, where, afterClipId, playheadSec, trackId): Copy clipIds and paste them in one undo step, the same as the editor paste dialog. where "after" inserts after the current main clip (afterClipId, or the same current-clip rules as insert_clip_after) and ripples later clips on the receiving track. where "end" puts them at the end of that clip's chain (or 0 with no current clip) and ripples. where "playhead" places them at playheadSec (required) without rippling; the call fails if any receiving track already has a clip in that gap (it does not slide or ripple). trackId sends compatible clips to that track (a track id from get_timeline); "new" creates a new compatible layer (overlay for ordinary video, never a second main). Without trackId, clips keep their original tracks. One undo step; returns the new clips.
- `add_clip`(assetId, startSec, trackId): Place a project media asset (id from get_timeline's "assets") at startSec, on trackId or the main track / a matching track. One undo step; returns the new clip.
- `even_split_words`(clipId): P47: invent evenly spaced word timings for a text/caption clip from its text and length (whitespace words, or characters for CJK). One undo step; returns the clip with words[].
- `set_caption_words`(clipId, words, mode, entrance): P47: set words [{ text, atSec }] on a text clip (seconds from the clip start; clamped in order). Pass mode "word-highlight" to keep one cue with karaoke highlighting, or "word-pop" to expand into one short clip per word (entrance pop|fade|slide-up). One undo step.
- `set_clip_mask`(clipId, mask): P49: set a visibility mask on an image, video or HTML clip (not text, not an effect). The mask multiplies that clip's alpha. It does not limit an effect such as blur (use applyTo for effect scope) and it does not change a tracker's box mask (set_track_mask). shape is rect, ellipse, linear (a split; rotation 0 keeps the top half), band (a strip / mirror bar of width w) or path. Coordinates are fractions of the source picture from the top-left, not of the frame. rect/ellipse: x,y centre, w,h size, rotation degrees clockwise, rect radius 0-0.5 of the smaller side. path: nodes [{ id, x, y, in?: {x,y}, out?: {x,y} }] with at least 3 points (closed; handles are Bezier offsets). feather 0-0.5 and expand -0.5 to 0.5 are fractions of the shorter side. invert and enabled (false bypasses). track is the name or id of a tracker on this same clip; lost and out-of-range frames hold the last found position and never invent one. keys and nodeKeys animate numbers (t in seconds from the clip start); path keys are by node id, so adding or deleting a point does not renumber the others. A bad or unclosed path is rejected and nothing changes. One undo step; returns the clip.
- `clear_clip_mask`(clipId): P49: remove the visibility mask from a clip (the tracker box mask, if any, stays). One undo step; returns the clip.
- `set_clip_version`(clipId, versionId): Pin one timeline clip to a version of its asset, or pass versionId null to follow the storyboard's current version (asset.selectedVersionId). Split halves and pasted copies of the same shot pick independently. One undo step; returns the clip.
- `delete_version`(assetId, versionId, fallbackVersionId): Remove one version of an asset (a shot take). Cannot delete the last remaining version. Clips pinned to it or currently showing it switch to fallbackVersionId (default: the shot's current version if that remains, else the newest remaining). Reports the affected clips. Stored media is dropped only if nothing else references it. One undo step.
- `word_align_prompt`(clipId, audioClipId) · read-only: P47: returns a copy-paste prompt that asks an external AI for word timings JSON for the caption clip (Dionysus does not call an AI). Optional audioClipId adds that clip's duration to the prompt. Paste the reply into set_caption_words.
- `set_track_caption_style`(trackId, mode, highlight, entrance): P60: set the Caption style of a text/subtitle track to none, word-highlight or word-pop. The style applies to every clip on that track (including clips added later and SRT imported or pasted onto it). Clips without words get an even split (spaces → words; CJK → characters). word-pop expands each cue into one short clip per word (entrance pop|fade|slide-up). highlight is optional { pending, current, spoken } each { color (#rrggbb), opacity 0–1, scale, weight 100–900 }; defaults match the previous look (pending opacity 0.4, current #20d5ec and scale +0.08, spoken = the clip colour). Preview and export use the same styles. Clips with a caption override are left alone. One undo step.
- `track_word_align_prompt`(trackId, audioClipId) · read-only: P60: returns one copy-paste prompt that lists every cue on the text track (id, text, start/end). Dionysus does not call an AI. Paste the reply (one JSON object covering all cues) into set_track_caption_words.
- `set_track_caption_words`(trackId, cues, json): P60: apply word timings to every caption on a text track in one undo step. Pass cues [{ id, words: [{ text, atSec }] }] matching every clip on the track, or json as the pasted AI reply (a { cues: [...] } object or a map of cue id → words). Times are seconds from each cue start and are clamped in order. Invalid JSON or a reply that skips a cue changes nothing.
- `attach_asset_version`(assetId, shotId, url, path, baseUrl, text, dataUrl, name, makeCurrent, mode): P62: add a version to a storyboard asset (assetId) or a shot's clip (shotId) from a file the page fetches itself, so the bytes never pass through the tool call. Give exactly one of url (https:, or http://localhost / http://127.0.0.1 for a local file server; it must send Access-Control-Allow-Origin for this site and, from a public page, Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true), path with baseUrl, text (inline HTML for an html clip) or dataUrl. The type comes from the asset (html, audio, video or image) and the file is checked like a manual upload: an HTML clip must pass the clip lint with the asset's bindings and params (a .zip package is accepted), audio and video must decode. makeCurrent (default true) makes the new version the one in use; mode "replace" overwrites the current version in place instead (RULE 75). name is stored as the version's model label. Returns versionId, mediaAssetId, bytes, durationSec for audio/video, width/height and warnings. One undo step.
- `attach_asset_versions`(items, baseUrl, pattern, type, ids, makeCurrent, mode, name): P62: attach_asset_version for many files in one call and ONE undo step (at most 200). Give items [{ assetId | shotId, url | path | text | dataUrl, name?, makeCurrent?, mode? }] with an optional shared baseUrl, or a pattern such as "audio/vo-{assetId}.mp3" (every storyboard asset, only those of type when given, e.g. type "audio") or "clips/{shotId}.mp4" (every shot), optionally limited to ids. Files are fetched four at a time. Returns { added, failed, results } with one entry per item in order (ok, versionId, durationSec, … or error); a failed item does not stop the others.
- `import_storyboard`(json, url, replace, keepUploads): P62: load storyboard JSON ("dionysus.storyboard/1") into the project without the Import screen, checked by the importer like a pasted file. Give json (the storyboard as an object or text) or url (fetched by the page; same URL rules as attach_asset_version). With no storyboard it creates one. When one exists, pass replace: true: the board becomes the imported JSON, matched by id, so assets and shots that keep their ids keep their uploaded versions and trims (ids missing from the JSON leave the board; their files stay in the media library); keepUploads: false starts over instead. A storyboard part ("part", or no "meta") is merged into the current board by id without replace. Invalid JSON changes nothing and returns the error list. One undo step. Then call send_to_timeline (mode "relayout" to re-time clips already placed).

## Optional

- [Format reference](https://ckfun0skf.github.io/dionysus-ai-video-editor/ai/STORYBOARD_FORMAT.md): the full specification, including importer warnings and errors
- [HTML clip package](https://ckfun0skf.github.io/dionysus-ai-video-editor/ai/HTML_CLIP_PACKAGE.md): the dionysus.htmlclip/1 single-file format for "html" assets (manifest, runtime contract, bindings, params, template). Create code → AI mode writes a new clip from this spec; Code Editor → Revise with AI revises an existing one. Dionysus does not call an AI.
- [Audio clip format](https://ckfun0skf.github.io/dionysus-ai-video-editor/ai/AUDIO_CLIP_FORMAT.md): the dionysus.audioclip/1 JSON for audio assets with "source": "json" (tempo, tracks, synths, drums, noise, sfx, fx, params, examples)
- [Open the app](https://ckfun0skf.github.io/dionysus-ai-video-editor/)
